headline: US EPA PFAS mandate by 2029 creating massive structural demand for activated carbon as the only scalable remediation solution.
reasoning: The US EPA has enforced regulations requiring water utility companies to reduce PFAS forever chemical levels to four parts per trillion by 2029 — equivalent to four drops in 20 Olympic-sized swimming pools. PFAS is linked to thyroid cancer and other cancers and accumulates in the human body without breaking down. Activated carbon is currently the only technology capable of filtering PFAS at scale, and demand is materially outstripping supply with no futures market or price transparency, making it an opaque but structurally favourable market.
quote: The US EPA is actually enforced these water utility companies by 2029 that they need to reduce the levels of forever chemicals and PFAS down to four parts per trillion by 2029. And the only way to do that currently on scale is by filtering the water, by using what's called activated carbon... The overall trend of activated carbon is certainly heading in the right direction. The demand is very much outstripping supply currently.
